note:
Landing copy for the root pages: who most likely arrives on each page from search, and what the page says to them first (owner direction, November 23, 2026: every landing page speaks to the person who is there). scripts/finalize_pages.py applies it: 'title', 'description' and 'h1' replace the page's own when given (h1 may hold
), and 'intro' and 'actions' fill the block in the page header. 'audience' records who the page is written for; it is not shown. Every intro must be true to what that page itself lists, with no counts of listings. State pages are written by scripts/build_state_pages.py and country pages by scripts/build_world_pages.py from their own data; 'states/index.html' is read there. 'iam' is the home page's 'I'm here as' chooser; each link opens a page or filter that already exists.

index.html.audience: Anyone with a disability, or helping someone who has one, who is not yet sure where to start.
index.html.intro: Wheelchair broken? Coverage denied? Need a ramp, a ride, help at home or an interpreter? You are not the only one. Pick your state and what you need, and we will show you who can help, what to have ready and what the rules say.

iam.label: Deaf, hard of hearing or DeafBlind
Parent of a child with a disability
Stuck at home without a ramp
Social worker, nurse or case manager

local-help.html.audience: Someone who wants a phone number for a program near them, often searching for their county.
local-help.html.title: Find disability programs near you, by state and county | Mobility Talk
local-help.html.intro: Looking for help close to home? Choose your state, your county if you like, and what you need. Each program shows who to call, what to have ready and a link to its own page, for every state, D.C. and the U.S. territories.

know-your-rights.html.audience: Someone who was turned away, let go, denied a home, a ride or a benefit, or treated unfairly because of a disability.
know-your-rights.html.intro: If an employer, landlord, school, hospital, airline or agency treated you unfairly because of a disability, find what happened to you below. Each situation says which office handles it, what to do first and, where the source states one, how long you have.

ramps-home-access.html.audience: Someone who cannot get in and out of their own home safely, or a family member arranging a ramp or bathroom change.
ramps-home-access.html.title: Ramps and home modifications: who pays and how to apply | Mobility Talk
ramps-home-access.html.description: Can't get in and out of your home safely? Who pays for or builds ramps and home changes: VA grants, Medicaid waivers, DD agencies and local programs.
ramps-home-access.html.intro: If steps stand between you and your own front door, or your bathroom no longer works for you, more than one program can pay for or build the changes. Start with the route that fits you, and get approval before any work begins.

actions.label: Find ramp and home programs near me

mobility-independence.html.audience: A wheelchair or mobility equipment user whose chair is broken or no longer fits, and people who back the right to repair.
mobility-independence.html.title: Wheelchair repair and the right to repair and adapt | Mobility Talk
mobility-independence.html.description: Wheelchair broken or no longer fits? Find repair and reuse programs, see where wheelchair repair laws stand, and ask your lawmakers for the right to repair.
mobility-independence.html.intro: When your wheelchair breaks or stops fitting you, daily life can stop with it. Find repair and reuse programs near you, see where wheelchair repair laws stand, and tell lawmakers what would help.

actions.label: Repair and reuse programs near me

mobility-rights.html.audience: A wheelchair or equipment user facing a stalled repair, a coverage denial, an inaccessible home, vehicle or bus, or a place that turned them away.
mobility-rights.html.title: Wheelchair repair, coverage denied or no ride? Your next step | Mobility Talk
mobility-rights.html.intro: Waiting weeks on a wheelchair repair, turned down for equipment, or unable to get on the bus? Choose your state and what is in the way. You will see what the rules say, questions to ask and a message you can make your own.

disability-advocacy.html.audience: A disabled person, family member or ally who wants to ask state or federal lawmakers for change.
disability-advocacy.html.title: Disability advocacy: ask lawmakers for repair, coverage and access | Mobility Talk
disability-advocacy.html.intro: Tired of waiting on repairs, coverage, a ride or an accessible home? Choose the change you want to see, learn who can act, and send your state or federal lawmakers a message in your own words.

blind-low-vision.html.audience: Someone who is blind, has low vision or is losing their sight, and their family.
blind-low-vision.html.intro: Blind, losing your sight, or helping someone who is? Start with the free national services, then find your state for its talking-book and braille library, help for older adults with vision loss and the other programs listed there.

deaf-hard-of-hearing.html.audience: Someone who is Deaf, hard of hearing or DeafBlind, and their family.
deaf-hard-of-hearing.html.intro: Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, or family of someone who is? Find relay and captioned calls, free phone equipment, your state's office for deaf and hard of hearing people, and iCanConnect equipment for DeafBlind people.

service-animals.html.audience: Someone who handles a service dog, is hoping to get one, or was told their dog is not allowed.
service-animals.html.intro: Have a service dog, or hoping to get one? Here is what staff may and may not ask, where your dog can go, your rights in rented housing and on planes, how to complain and where to find a trained dog. Each statement links to the official source it comes from.

actions.label: The two questions staff may ask

caregiver-respite.html.audience: A family member or friend looking after someone with a disability or illness, including a veteran, who needs a break or more help.
caregiver-respite.html.intro: Looking after a family member, friend or veteran with a disability or illness, and in need of a break? Find respite near you, the public programs that help caregivers, and how some families get paid for care. Each statement links to the official page it comes from.

accessible-vehicles.html.audience: A wheelchair user, a driver with a disability or a family member who needs an accessible van, hand controls or a lift and is looking for help paying.
accessible-vehicles.html.intro: Need a wheelchair accessible van, hand controls or a lift, and wondering who helps pay? Here is the order that saves money, VA grants, vocational rehabilitation, Medicaid waivers, automaker rebates, loans and tax help. Each statement links to the official page it comes from.

free-medical-equipment.html.audience: Someone who needs a wheelchair, walker, hospital bed or other equipment, or a repair, and cannot afford it or cannot wait.
free-medical-equipment.html.intro: Need a wheelchair, walker or other equipment and cannot afford it or cannot wait? Borrow it, get it used, or find out what Medicare, Medicaid, the VA and equipment grants will pay, including repairs. Each statement links to the official page it comes from.

social-security-disability.html.audience: A person who cannot work because of a disability or illness, or a family member helping them, who wants to apply for SSDI or SSI or was turned down.
social-security-disability.html.intro: Cannot work because of a disability or illness? Here is how Social Security disability works: SSDI or SSI, how it decides who qualifies, what to gather, what happens after you apply and how to appeal a denial. Each statement links to the Social Security page it comes from.

accessible-travel.html.audience: A wheelchair user or other traveler with a disability, or a family member, planning a flight, a train or bus trip, or a national park visit.
accessible-travel.html.intro: Planning a trip with a wheelchair or another disability? Here is what airlines must do for you, how to get help at airport security, how to book accessible space on Amtrak and intercity buses, and how to get the free Access Pass for national parks. Each statement links to the official page it comes from.

paid-family-caregiver.html.audience: A spouse, adult child, parent or friend who gives a disabled or older family member daily care and wants to know whether they can be paid for it.
paid-family-caregiver.html.intro: Caring for a parent, spouse or child at home and wondering if you can be paid for it? Here is what actually exists: Medicaid programs that let the person hire you, Structured Family Caregiving in some states, the VA caregiver stipend, Veteran-Directed Care and Aid and Attendance, long-term care insurance, paid leave and the tax rules. Each statement links to the official page it comes from.

home-modifications.html.audience: A person with a disability or an older adult, or a family member, who needs a ramp, a stairlift, a safer bathroom or wider doors at home and wants help paying for it.
home-modifications.html.intro: Need a ramp, a stairlift, grab bars or wider doors at home? Here is who helps pay: VA grants and HISA, USDA repair loans and grants, Medicaid waivers, Area Agencies on Aging, state assistive technology programs, and the tax rules if you pay yourself. Each statement links to the official page it comes from, with current dollar limits.

disability-housing.html.audience: A person with a disability, or a family member, who needs affordable or accessible rental housing, is searching for Section 8 or other housing help, or was refused a change they need by a landlord.
disability-housing.html.intro: Looking for affordable or accessible housing with a disability? Here is how Section 8 vouchers treat a disability, the Mainstream and NED vouchers for people under 62, Section 811 supportive housing, your rights in public housing, USDA rural rentals, how to file a fair housing complaint, and help with energy bills. Each statement links to the official page it comes from.

disability-jobs.html.audience: A person with a disability who wants to work or keep working, including people on SSDI or SSI who worry about losing benefits, and family members helping them.
disability-jobs.html.intro: Want to work with a disability without losing the help you count on? Here is what vocational rehabilitation pays for and how to apply, Ticket to Work, Social Security’s work rules with the 2026 and 2027 amounts, ABLE accounts, Schedule A federal hiring, your right to accommodations, and free benefits counseling. Each statement links to the official page it comes from.

disability-parking.html.audience: A person whose disability limits walking, or a family member or driver, who needs a disability parking placard or plates, wants to renew one, or is driving to another state.
disability-parking.html.intro: Need a disability parking placard or plates? Here is who qualifies, placard or plates, temporary and long-term placards, what your medical provider certifies, renewal, using a placard in another state, disabled veteran plates, what the ADA requires of the spaces, and a link to each state’s official placard page. Each statement links to the official page it comes from.

vehiculos-adaptados.html.audience: Una persona que usa silla de ruedas, o su familia, que prefiere leer en español y busca ayuda para pagar un vehículo adaptado o controles manuales.
vehiculos-adaptados.html.intro: ¿Necesita una camioneta adaptada para silla de ruedas, controles manuales o un elevador? Aquí está quién puede ayudar a pagar: el VA, la rehabilitación vocacional, Medicaid, los fabricantes de autos, préstamos e impuestos. Cada afirmación indica la página oficial de donde proviene.

equipo-medico-gratis.html.audience: Una persona que necesita una silla de ruedas, una andadera u otro equipo médico, o su familia, que prefiere leer en español.
equipo-medico-gratis.html.intro: ¿Necesita una silla de ruedas, una andadera u otro equipo y no puede pagarlo? Aquí está cómo pedirlo prestado, conseguirlo usado o recibir ayuda de Medicare, Medicaid, el VA o una subvención. Cada afirmación indica la página oficial de donde proviene.

incapacidad-seguro-social.html.audience: Una persona que no puede trabajar por una discapacidad o enfermedad, o un familiar que le ayuda, que prefiere leer en español.
incapacidad-seguro-social.html.intro: ¿No puede trabajar por una discapacidad o enfermedad? Aquí está cómo funcionan los beneficios por incapacidad del Seguro Social: SSDI o SSI, cómo decide quién califica, qué reunir, qué pasa después de solicitar y cómo apelar una negación. Cada afirmación indica la página del Seguro Social de donde proviene.

cuidador-familiar-pagado.html.audience: Un cónyuge, hijo, hija, padre, madre o amigo que cuida todos los días a un familiar con discapacidad o mayor, que prefiere leer en español y quiere saber si puede recibir pago por hacerlo.
cuidador-familiar-pagado.html.intro: ¿Cuida en casa a su padre, su madre, su pareja o su hijo y se pregunta si le pueden pagar por hacerlo? Aquí está lo que existe: programas de Medicaid que permiten que la persona le contrate, el Cuidado Familiar Estructurado en algunos estados, el estipendio del VA para cuidadores, la Atención Dirigida por el Veterano y Ayuda y Asistencia, el seguro de cuidado a largo plazo, las licencias del trabajo y los impuestos. Cada afirmación indica la página oficial de donde proviene.

modificaciones-hogar.html.audience: Una persona con discapacidad o una persona mayor, o su familia, que prefiere leer en español y necesita una rampa, un salvaescaleras, un baño más seguro o puertas más anchas en casa.
modificaciones-hogar.html.intro: ¿Necesita en casa una rampa, un salvaescaleras, barras de agarre o puertas más anchas? Aquí está quién ayuda a pagar: las subvenciones del VA y HISA, los préstamos y subvenciones del USDA para reparaciones, las exenciones de Medicaid, las Agencias del Área sobre el Envejecimiento, los programas estatales de tecnología de asistencia y las reglas de impuestos si lo paga usted. Cada afirmación indica la página oficial de donde proviene, con los límites actuales en dólares.

vivienda-discapacidad.html.audience: Una persona con discapacidad, o su familia, que prefiere leer en español y necesita una vivienda de alquiler asequible o accesible, busca la Sección 8 u otra ayuda de vivienda, o a quien un arrendador le negó un cambio que necesita.
vivienda-discapacidad.html.intro: ¿Busca una vivienda asequible o accesible y tiene una discapacidad? Aquí está cómo la Sección 8 trata una discapacidad, los vales Mainstream y NED para personas menores de 62 años, la vivienda con apoyo de la Sección 811, sus derechos en la vivienda pública, los alquileres rurales del USDA, cómo presentar una queja de vivienda justa y la ayuda con las facturas de energía. Cada afirmación indica la página oficial de donde proviene.

empleo-discapacidad.html.audience: Una persona con discapacidad que prefiere leer en español y quiere trabajar o seguir trabajando, incluidas las personas que reciben SSDI o SSI y temen perder sus beneficios, y los familiares que les ayudan.
empleo-discapacidad.html.intro: ¿Quiere trabajar con una discapacidad sin perder la ayuda con la que cuenta? Aquí está lo que paga la rehabilitación vocacional y cómo solicitarla, el Boleto para Trabajar, las reglas de trabajo del Seguro Social con las cantidades de 2026 y 2027, las cuentas ABLE, la contratación federal por Schedule A, su derecho a adaptaciones y la asesoría de beneficios gratuita. Cada afirmación indica la página oficial de donde proviene.

estacionamiento-discapacidad.html.audience: Una persona con una discapacidad que limita su capacidad para caminar, o un familiar o un conductor, que prefiere leer en español y necesita un permiso o placas de estacionamiento por discapacidad, quiere renovarlos o va a manejar a otro estado.
estacionamiento-discapacidad.html.intro: ¿Necesita un permiso o placas de estacionamiento por discapacidad? Aquí está quién califica, la diferencia entre el permiso y las placas, los permisos temporales y a largo plazo, lo que certifica su proveedor médico, cómo renovar, cómo usar su permiso en otro estado, las placas para veteranos discapacitados, lo que exige la ADA de los espacios y un enlace a la página oficial de permisos de cada estado. Cada afirmación indica la página oficial de donde proviene.

espanol.html.audience: Una persona con discapacidad, o su familia, que prefiere recibir ayuda en español.
espanol.html.intro: ¿Usted o alguien de su familia tiene una discapacidad y prefiere recibir ayuda en español? Estas líneas nacionales atienden en español o tienen información en español. Ocho guías también están en español; el resto del sitio está en inglés por ahora.

world.html.audience: A disabled person or family living outside the United States.
world.html.intro: Living with a disability outside the United States, or helping someone who is? Choose your country for where to start, disability payments, equipment and who handles discrimination, each checked against official pages, with the emergency number and a crisis line on every page.

actions.label: Help that works in any country

states/index.html.audience: Someone who searched for disability resources in their state and wants the whole list in one place.
states/index.html.intro: Choose your state on the map or in the list. Each state page groups its programs by what you need, with phone numbers and a link to each program's own page.
